subject: Precomputing neighbourhood quantities in a custom NIMBLE distribution

messages.author: 4f5ed50c5c0ea3d1
messages.subject: Precomputing neighbourhood quantities in a custom NIMBLE distribution
parts:
Dear NIMBLE users,

I am developing the R package nimbleTools, available on GitHub (https://github.com/bsmiguelangel/nimbleTools). The package includes tools to run NIMBLE models in parallel, diagnose MCMC output, and use a custom Leroux CAR distribution in NIMBLE model code. I am planning to submit it to CRAN and would first like to improve the way neighbourhood information is provided to this distribution. Currently, my dcar_leroux() function is defined as follows:

dcar_leroux <- nimble::nimbleFunction(
  name = "dcar_leroux",
  run = function(x = double(1),                      # Spatial random effect (vector)
                 rho = double(0),                    # Amount of spatial dependence (scalar)
                 sd = double(0),                     # Standard deviation (scalar)
                 Lambda = double(1),                 # Eigenvalues of matrix D - W
                 from.to = double(2),                # Matrix of distinct pairs of neighbours from.to[, 1] < from.to[, 2]
                 zero_mean = double(0, default = 0), # Apply zero-mean constraint when set to 1
                 log = integer(0, default = 0)) {

    # Number of small areas
    NAreas <- dim(x)[1]

    # Number of distinct pairs of neighbours
    NDist <- dim(from.to)[1]

    # Required vectors
    from <- nimInteger(NDist)
    to <- nimInteger(NDist)
    x.from <- nimNumeric(NDist)
    x.to <- nimNumeric(NDist)

    for (Dist in 1:NDist) {
      from[Dist] <- ADbreak(from.to[Dist, 1])
      to[Dist] <- ADbreak(from.to[Dist, 2])
      x.from[Dist] <- x[from[Dist]]
      x.to[Dist] <- x[to[Dist]]
    }

    logDens <- sum(dnorm(x[1:NAreas], mean = 0, sd = sd * pow(1 - rho, -1/2), log = TRUE)) -
      NAreas/2 * log(1 - rho) + sum(log(rho * (Lambda[1:NAreas] - 1) + 1))/2 -
      pow(sd, -2) * rho * sum(pow(x.from[1:NDist] - x.to[1:NDist], 2))/2

    # Add a zero-mean constraint when requested
    if (zero_mean == 1) {
      logDens <- logDens + dnorm(mean(x[1:NAreas]),
                                 mean = 0,
                                 sd = sd / (10 * pow(NAreas, 1/2)),
                                 log = TRUE)
    }

    returnType(double(0))
    if (log) {
      return(logDens)
    } else {
      return(exp(logDens))
    }

  },
  buildDerivs = list(run = list(ignore = c("Dist", "NAreas", "NDist")))
)

Here, Lambda contains the eigenvalues of the matrix D-W, while from.to is a two-column matrix containing the distinct pairs of neighbouring areas. I currently have a separate R function, lerouxObjects(), which constructs these two objects from a binary adjacency matrix, the usual adj and num neighbourhood representation, or a graph. Thus, users must first calculate Lambda and from.to and then provide them explicitly in the model:

theta[1:NAreas] ~ dcar_leroux(rho = rho,
                              sd = sd,
                              Lambda = Lambda[1:NAreas],
                              from.to = from.to[1:NDist, 1:2],
                              zero_mean = 0)

What I would like to achieve is a simpler interface, similar to that of the CAR distributions available in NIMBLE, where users provide the neighbourhood information directly:

theta[1:NAreas] ~ dcar_leroux(rho = rho,
                              sd = sd,
                              adj = adj[1:NAdj],
                              num = num[1:NAreas],
                              zero_mean = 0)

Internally, the distribution would calculate Lambda and from.to from adj and num, and then use them to evaluate exactly the same log-density as before. The important requirement is that these calculations should be performed only once, before MCMC sampling begins, rather than every time the log-density is evaluated. I would also like to preserve compatibility with automatic differentiation and HMC, which already work with the current implementation.

Is there a recommended way in NIMBLE to handle this kind of preprocessing for a user-defined distribution while keeping the usual dcar_leroux() syntax?

I would appreciate any suggestions on the most appropriate approach.

Thank you very much for your help.

Best regards,  
Miguel Ángel

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Precomputing neighbourhood quantities in a custom NIMBLE distribution
parts:
Hi Miguel Ángel,
This sounds interesting. Thanks for the question.
Here are a couple of potential options:
1. It is now possible for a user-defined distribution to hold its own variables and state information. This is done by creating it from a nimbleFunction with setup code. The change is that you would have to use it in the model something like `leroux$dcar`, i.e. as a method of an object. This is described in section 13.3 of the user manual. This approach could allow you to have users provide whatever format is natural when they create the `leroux` object and then and have a one-time calculation (in setup code) to create whatever other form of information you need for repeated (log) density calls.
2. Another option would be relevant if you are providing a custom sampler to go with dcar_leroux. In that case, you could provide a `before_chain` method for the sampler that does the one-time calculations you need and stores them in the sampler. The differences from above would be: (i) The info is just in one sampler, so is not available for other uses of the model, and (ii) the one-time calculations would be done each time you start an MCMC.
HTH. Let us know any follow-up questions or if these aren't suited to your purpose.
Perry
